title: Lincoln's Niagara speech on the giants whose bones fill the mounds

tellings.quote: Abraham Lincoln who's waxing poetically about Niagara Falls in a speech in which he says, "The eyes of that ancient species of giants whose bones fill the mounds of America have gazed upon Niagara as ours do."

plain: Abraham Lincoln, writing about Niagara Falls, is quoted as saying, "The eyes of that ancient species of giants whose bones fill the mounds of America have gazed upon Niagara as ours do." Tim Alberino, a researcher who says giants once lived on earth, brings up the passage to Michels without saying where he found it, as a sign that Lincoln's America took giant bones in the old burial mounds for granted. Alberino himself says Lincoln was "waxing poetically" here, so the line shows what Lincoln wrote, but it leaves open whether he meant the giants literally or as a figure of speech.
